name: Screened conductor
summary: A single conductor enclosed by a drawn screen outline, showing that the core has a conductive shield around it.
description: A screened conductor symbol adds an outline around one conductor to show a conductive screen, braid or foil surrounding the core. It is used for analogue instrument signals, encoder and thermocouple extension wiring and other circuits where capacitively coupled interference must be kept off the signal.

The outline alone does not show where or whether the screen is earthed. Earthing at one end, both ends or through a capacitor is a design decision that should be drawn explicitly with an earth or bonding symbol at the screen tail. The symbol also does not distinguish foil, braid or combined screens, which belong in the cable schedule.
readingNotes: Find the screen tail and confirm where it is terminated.
Check whether a cable marker applies to the screened core and any others in the same cable.
drawingChecklist: Show the screen termination point explicitly.
Record the screen type in the cable schedule.
Keep screen drain terminals numbered on the terminal plan.
distinction: A screened conductor has a conductive shield; a cable-core grouping outline only shows that several cores share one sheath and implies no shielding.
